title: Understanding Dynamic Routes in Next.js
author: Tad MacPherson
contentHtml:
A file named [id].js can represent many pages. The value in the URL becomes the id parameter, which lets one component display different posts.

For this blog, each JSON record becomes a possible route. The post named dynamic-routes can be opened at /posts/dynamic-routes.

title: Two Forms of Pre-rendering
author: Tad MacPherson
contentHtml:
Next.js has two forms of pre-rendering: Static Generation and Server-side Rendering. The difference is in when it generates the HTML for a page.

  • Static Generation creates HTML at build time and reuses it for requests.
  • Server-side Rendering creates HTML on each request.

Next.js lets each page choose the approach that fits its data.

title: Choosing Between SSG and SSR
author: Tad MacPherson
contentHtml:
Static generation is a strong choice when content can be prepared ahead of time. Server-side rendering is better when a page must use fresh data for every request.

A blog post is usually a good candidate for static generation. A dashboard showing a live account balance would be a better candidate for server-side rendering.

title: Building Pages Ahead of Time
author: Tad MacPherson
contentHtml:
Static generation gives a page its HTML before a visitor requests it. That can make a content-focused site fast and dependable.

The page can still receive post data through getStaticProps during the build.

title: A Practical Rendering Decision
author: Tad MacPherson
contentHtml:
The best rendering strategy depends on how often the data changes and whether each request needs a different result.

Understanding that tradeoff helps a Next.js application stay both simple and responsive.
